body.p: Claims 2-24 are pending. Claims 2 and 6 have been amended. Claim 1 was previously cancelled, and claims 25 and 26 have been currently cancelled without prejudice to or disclaimer of the subject matter therein. No new matter has been added.
body.h1: STATEMENT OF SUBSTANCE REGARDING EXAMINER INTERVIEW
body.p: Applicant thanks the Examiner for the Applicant-initiated Interview conducted on December 19, 2024. During the Interview, the participants discussed a proposed amendment similar to the one presented herein. The Examiner agreed that the amendment would overcome the current rejections and that further searching would be performed. The Interview then ended.
CLAIM REJECTION UNDER 35 U.S.C. § 103
Claims 2-26 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2007/0299473 (Matos) in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2011/0018998 (Guzik), and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2011/0092825 (Gopinathan). Applicant does not acquiesce to this rejection.
Claim 2 has been amended to clarify its claimed subject matter. For example, claim 2 recites:
at least one processor communicatively coupled with the video camera, the data collection unit and the communications unit, the at least one processor configured
to:
establish at least one of a cellular or a wireless communication channel with the remote location,
transmit the acquired one or more still images of the subject to the remote location,
transmit the real-time video of the subject to the remote location,
determine an available bandwidth of the communication channel,
in response to the available bandwidth exceeding a predetermined threshold bandwidth, transmit the ECG
signals, SpO2 levels and blood pressure of the subject to the
remote location, and

p.u: in response to the available bandwidth not exceeding the predetermined threshold bandwidth, halt transmission of the real-time video of the sub
remote location and transmit the ECG signals
levels and blood pressure of the subject to the remote

body.p: As discussed during the Interview, and agreed upon with the Examiner, none of the references disclose or reasonably suggest the noted features. On page 9 of the Office action, the Office indicates that the concept of halting the transmission of video when the bandwidth is too low is taught by Matos at paragraph [1710]. However, this paragraph only discloses manually adjusting the framerate of video based on bandwidth availability, and does not disclose halting the transmission of video.
For at least the reasons provided above, a prima facie case of obviousness

cannot be established. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 2 be reconsidered and withdrawn. Also, dependent claims 3-24 should also be found allowable, at least based on their dependence from claim 1, as well as for their additional distinguishing features.
